notes.title: Solateria Development Note #3 - Refinement of Core Game Systems
notes.content:
[p]Hello Pyron Warriors, this is Studio Doodal.  
We are greeting you with our third development note.

June and July have brought many internal changes to the game. The long-awaited Parts System has finally started functioning, we have created the key feature of the game, the Core Stone, and the operation of the Heat Core has also been updated.


[/p][h1]1. Core Stone[/h1][p]
In Solateria, there are Core Stones that allow players to use the Heat Resistance they gain during gameplay to grow the protagonist. Players can enhance their chosen Core Stones with Heat Resistance to develop the protagonist according to their own style. Core Stones can also be engraved to hold even more Heat Resistance.

With a single Core Stone able to enhance multiple stats, and each Core Stone having a distinct role, players can cultivate their character based on their preferred playstyle.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/c610fe1cf9149f72b59c73bffbdbbc53c25561cf.png"][/img][/p][p]▲ A part of the Core Stone UI.


[/p][h1]2. Completion of Various Parts[/h1][p]
Alongside the Core Stone, the Parts System that allows players to customize the protagonist to their liking has been completed.

The protagonist can equip four types of parts: Attack, Defense, Heat, and Warmhorn. Each part has unique effects that add variety to gameplay.

Through various part combinations, you can now experience battles in your very own style.


[/p][h1]3. Heat Core[/h1][p]
The Heat Core System introduced in our previous development note has also undergone adjustments.

Previously, increasing the Heat Core mainly required parrying. However, collecting enough Heat Core demanded too many parries, and the skills that consumed the collected Heat Core were not as powerful as expected.

We wanted Heat Core skills to serve as a kind of “ultimate ability” that could be used strategically in the right moments, so we decided to focus more on this role.

Therefore, Heat Cores can now only be recharged at Altars, but in return, players can unleash more powerful skills. This change allows you to use the limited Heat Core strategically to escape dangerous situations.  
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/64e0b5bc24e684602bd233f74fe924b2c19d61be.gif"][/img]▲ Rest at an Altar to recharge your Heat Core and Warmhorn!


[/p][h1]4. Ashfire Library[/h1][p]
We believe the Ashfire Library will become one of the most frequently visited locations during your exploration of Solateria.

Located atop the Ashen Hills, the library has been carefully designed with the player’s movement and convenience in mind.  
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/c33bcd92c040fdc9292797efd2c45729c8973f8b.png"][/img]While all the important NPCs and functions are centralized, exploring every corner of the library may lead to unexpected rewards.  
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/b200006b786969e27f6de7ca519aa5bd805cff8d.gif"][/img][/p][p]▲ This is Verita, the librarian who manages the library.


[/p][h1]5. Adjustment of Creature Attack Motions[/h1][p]
As mentioned in the previous development note, Solateria focuses on parry-based combat.

Believing that parrying is the most crucial element, we have refined all creature attack motions and timings to make parries more intuitive and precise.

Our goal is to deliver an even sharper and more rhythmic parrying experience.


[/p][h1]6. Tutorial Boss – Charon’s Appearance Cutscene Update[/h1][p]
Before the player’s first encounter with Charon, our intended player behavior was: “There’s a dangerous river ahead, so let’s turn back.”

After realizing the river is impassable, the player would turn back and suddenly encounter Charon emerging from the river.

However, from various exhibition feedback, we noticed that many players simply fell into the river and died, then revived at an Altar and wandered off elsewhere.

To prevent players from getting lost, we redesigned Charon’s encounter conditions. How exactly Charon now appears will be something you’ll have to experience in the game!  
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/83600843497be9dbadbcc78d8888edeef52a1b1d.png"][/img]

[/p][h1]7. Item Box[/h1][p]
Item Boxes containing important items have been added.

While regular items will still be scattered in the field, Item Boxes will offer more significant items. Explore the world of Solateria to find hidden Item Boxes and claim valuable items!  
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/1955f1f04279aeef846ec518862ff484053ed590.gif"][/img]

This concludes our third development note.  
Thank you.[/p]

notes.title: Solateria Devlog #2 – The Process of Implementing Parry-Focused Action
notes.content:
[p]Hello Pyron Warriors, this is Studio Doodal.  
We greet you with our second development log.[/p][p] [/p][p]From May 21st to 25th, we showcased a new demo build of Solateria at the “PlayX4” exhibition!  
We sincerely thank all the players who came to try Solateria.  
We carefully reviewed each piece of feedback shared at the site, along with about 100 survey responses,  
and we are striving to create a better game based on that feedback.[/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/d15eb3e39f48b9544864b39e08f350f86f54c1df.jpg"][/img][/p][p]
[/p][p]The first public reveal of Solateria was last July, around six months into development,  
at the “Bitsummit” exhibition held in Japan.  
The build showcased at this PlayX4 had many significant differences from the one a year ago.  
Fortunately, compared to the feedback we received last year,  
we got far more positive responses this time—  
confirming that the direction Studio Doodal has been pursuing is the right one.[/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/2bee19e61a103927cdb7ce883d70bb12e05198f6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]
[/p][p]Since we first revealed Solateria at Bitsummit in July,  
there have been about three major system changes.  
The process has been long and difficult.[/p][p]
[/p][p]In this development log, we’ll talk about the changes Solateria has undergone so far,  
and the biggest differences between the latest PlayX4 build and previous builds.[/p][p]
[/p][h2]1. The Process of Creating Parry-Focused Action[/h2][p]
[/p][p]“With so many metroidvania and action games out there,  
how can Solateria have its own distinct action mechanics?”  
This was the question we asked ourselves from the very beginning of development.  
And each time we showcased the game offline, we closely observed how players engaged with it and continued to refine our answer.[/p][p]
[/p][p]Our conclusion was this: Solateria focuses on ‘parry-based combat’,  
and since the protagonist is the flame-attribute warrior Blue Flame,  
we built the game around ‘skills related to fire and heat’ as its defining features.[/p][h3]Problems Identified at Various Exhibitions[/h3][p]The build shown at last year’s Bitsummit, Tokyo Game Show, BIC, G-Star, and G-Eight was centered on parrying mechanics.  
However, many players gave up on parrying after just a few attempts and shifted to dodge-heavy play styles.  
At G-Star, we collected 844 surveys and analyzed the results thoroughly.  
As a result, our development team concluded: “There is a lack of reward for parrying.”[/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/bf736864840083067457f17a660332e9e0f0745b.png"][/img][/p][p]
[/p][h3]Additional Rewards for Parrying[/h3][p]It’s good to allow players to freely choose their methods—be it parry, guard, or dodge—when fighting bosses.  
However, Solateria was fundamentally built upon parry-centric gameplay, and we wanted the joy of parrying to be felt most during boss battles.  
In the previous build, rewards were only granted when a specific enemy pattern was parried.  
This meant very few players experienced the intended parry rewards.  
So, the system we had designed remained mostly unseen.[/p][p]
[/p][p]We redesigned the system so that the skill “Pyron Action,” previously usable only after parrying specific patterns, could be activated more frequently.  
We added “Stun Points” to all creatures—parrying would reduce these points, and once they hit zero, Pyron Action would be triggered.  
This made the parry–counter loop occur more often during combat.[/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/bbe3032c853896be40acc934382fcb3aab1a130f.gif"][/img][/p][p]
[/p][p]In the original tutorial, you had to parry a specific 3-hit combo to access Pyron Action guidance.  
Now, all tutorial enemies have 1 Stun Point.  
So if you parry just once, you immediately get to use Pyron Action.  
This change lets players easily experience the core mechanic early on.[/p][p]
[/p][p]In boss fights, the intended flow is: parry to reduce Stun Points → trigger Pyron Action → build up parries and attacks → make the boss groggy → unleash the powerful skill, “Burst.”[/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/95eaa3ac10ae98697ce093e4c39e3d6e0985cf10.gif"][/img][/p][p]
[/p][h3]Heat Core – Highlighting the Flame Warrior’s Identity[/h3][p]To match the flame warrior concept, we added a new system called “Heat Core.”  
There are many factors that increase or decrease Heat Core,  
but the most basic is a successful parry.  
You can unlock up to five stages of Heat Core, each providing powerful skills that support gameplay.[/p][p]
[/p][p]Originally, the second-stage Heat Core placed a fire field that dealt damage over time and added bonus hits to attacks.  
But many players said it didn’t feel effective.  
So we redesigned the skills at each stage to be more intuitive and impactful.[/p][p]
[/p][p]For example, the second-stage Heat Core now fires strong flame attacks forward and backward.  
This scorches all visible enemies on the screen and inflicts burn status.  
The skill also grants temporary invincibility, giving players a moment to use potions if needed.[/p][p]
[/p][p]-Heat Core Stage 2 (Before):[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/4972c21e62c8f1ae338be5c1e9254a1478314074.gif"][/img][/p][p]-Heat Core Stage 2 (After):[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/6e42aafb509cf85b7d4a3cac3e8f9a13d4b8a73b.gif"][/img][/p][p]
[/p][p]As the stages increase, parrying contributes more significantly to Heat Core, increasing the value of parry in gameplay.[/p][p]
[/p][p]We revealed this updated build at last month’s PlayX4.  
Many players who experienced Pyron Action shifted from dodge-focused to parry-centric play.  
After a long journey, it was fulfilling to see that the gameplay direction we aimed for matched the fun players experienced.[/p][h2]2. Efforts to Improve Hit and Damage Feedback[/h2][p]
[/p][p]To address the often-mentioned issue of lackluster hit/damage feedback at last year’s events,  
we significantly amplified the black bleeding effect, made enemies flash white briefly on hit, and added screen shake.  
We also improved the SFX.  
Knockback was considered, but in Solateria’s combat system—where characters can overlap with creatures—  
adding knockback proved structurally difficult.  
Instead, we polished the game to deliver satisfying hit feedback without knockback.[/p][p][/p][p]We also enlarged the visual effects triggered by successful parries,  
clearly differentiating them from guard effects.  
These changes led to significantly more positive feedback regarding hit and damage feel at PlayX4. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/cbb00db43ecffbc6634a999ecd92110334babae6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]– (Left) Previous Parry Effect, (Right) Current Parry Effect[/p][p]
[/p][h2]3. Extensive Art Polish to Match the Game's Atmosphere[/h2][p][/p][p]Are you familiar with Studio Doodal’s previous title?[/p][p]Our first game was LAPIN, a charming — yet challenging — precision platformer. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/97646ebaca1919f7ec15a5820357d0cc23f45f34.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/4a1be36b5fa5e4d97da56e55244823da63f0dba4.png"][/img][/p][p]
Because we were used to designing cute visuals, the early creature concepts for Solateria also had a somewhat cute look.[/p][p]
[/p][p]– Early Creature Design: [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/8dcb38d65a7802748bd5f842935b742c604e621a.png"][/img][/p][p]We initially aimed to maintain the beautiful hand-drawn art style of LAPIN,  
which made the overall tone of the game quite bright. [/p][p]However, through various exhibitions, we realized that this bright, cute art style didn’t match the dark story of Solateria.  
So, we worked hard to shift toward a darker aesthetic and redesigned many previously created creatures.[/p][p][/p][p]– Redesigned Creature Design:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/31b48e0c6df8c80ae6d284820b3374b963d62c77.jpg"][/img][/p][p]
As a result, we were able to create artwork that much more closely matches the atmosphere of the Solateria universe.[/p][p]
[/p][p]— Studio Doodal[/p][p]
[/p][previewyoutube="nXPu4_aKVQs;full"][/previewyoutube][hr][/hr][p]

[/p]

notes.title: Solateria Dev Log #01
notes.content:
Hello Pyron Warriors,

Since we began developing Solateria in January last year, this is our first time greeting you through a development log.
From now on, we plan to share monthly updates so that you can follow the game’s progress and improvements with us.

After showcasing our early build at various exhibitions, we’ve made major improvements:
We added clear rewards for parrying and restructured the gameplay to better support parry-focused combat.
We also introduced the Heat System to further reflect the identity of the flame warrior.

Additionally, we refined the creature designs, rebalanced background tones, and created new cutscenes.
Your feedback—both online and offline—made these changes possible, and we thank you for it.

This current build is vastly different from the one shown before.
We hope to share it with you soon. Now, let’s begin the April development log.


[h1][Solateria – Development Log #01][/h1]

[h2]1. New Cutscenes[/h2]
We focused on a variety of cinematic scenes this month—
From narrative moments with NPCs in beautiful landscapes, to dramatic boss deaths and wave finales.
We’ll first reveal a new cutscene from the Ashen Library, a safe haven for warriors who survived the Shadow Plague.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/9647a363f73cef8038132e12c9cd811bb5d2a1d7.gif[/img]

[h2]2. Parts System[/h2]
We’ve added a parts system to let you tailor your build:
Attack, Defense, Heat, and Wormhorn parts each offer unique enhancements, such as bonus damage under low health or persistent effects.
Equip one part of each type to customize your combat experience and explore more playstyles.

[h2]3. Heat System[/h2]
To highlight the Pyron identity, we added the Heat System, which allows warriors to channel their inner fire.
Unlockable in five tiers, this system enables special abilities in combat depending on your current heat level—
And at full charge, you’ll gain access to a powerful finisher.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/5fd3e85f3f94c137476ead0cffd7030f28f5a458.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/4972c21e62c8f1ae338be5c1e9254a1478314074.gif[/img]

That’s it for April’s development log.
Thank you always for playing Solateria, and we’ll see you again in next month’s update.
- Studio Doodal

notes.title: Solateria Participates in BitSummit 2024 in Kyoto!
notes.content:
Dear Pyron Warriors.

 

Studio Doodal's upcoming title, the 2D action Metroidvania game <Solateria>, participated in the BitSummit event held in Kyoto, Japan, last July.

It was a valuable opportunity to meet many Japanese players and receive their invaluable feedback.

We also took part in a live broadcast at the BitSummit event, where we had the chance to introduce Solateria to the live audience.

Youtube Link : https://www.youtube.com/live/Y9BTQ90V0b4?si=P4njL2dA2mlZcJN4&t=6542

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45076914/9ad35b9b82f695f2ec9ec790dded99853a9d255a.jpg[/img]

Additionally, we conducted an interview about Solateria with 4Gamer, one of Japan's leading magazines!

Article Link : https://www.4gamer.net/games/820/G082045/20240719072/


The article titled, "Interview with the Developer of the Souls-like 2D Action Game Solateria: Creating a Beautiful Hand-drawn Game World with College Friends," beautifully portrays the origins of Studio Doodal, which began during our university days.

We look forward to meeting you at many more international events in the future.


Sincerely,
Studio Doodal
